evidence.source: Wiktionary, 高 entry (pronunciation table citing Zhengzhang 2003)
evidence.text: The entry gives Standard Mandarin gāo (Pinyin), Cantonese gou1 (Jyutping), Middle Chinese kaw in its reconstruction table, and Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese *kaːw. The page also separately reports Baxter–Sagart *Cə.[k]ˤaw; these are reconstructions of the word represented by 高, not evidence for any sound component, since the graph is described there as pictographic.

gaps: No primary inscription context was verified that securely establishes the earliest lexical sense of 高; catalogued oracle-bone and bronze forms establish graphic witnesses, but not a semantic chain.

The proposed pictograph of a tall building or raised tower is supported by the Shuowen account and modern dictionary descriptions. The actual depicted architecture and details of graphic change across the early forms remain unverified because candidate image fetches failed and no glyph pixels were inspected.

The Shuowen segmentation into 冂 and 口 is a historical lexicographic analysis. Separate original semantic contributions for those shapes are not independently established; no phonetic component is proposed.
No whole-graph borrowing claim was located. The comparisons to 京 and proposed lexical links to 喬 or 浩 do not establish shared graphic ancestry or borrowing; those relations remain unresolved.

The Ministry dictionary cites early classical-text uses for high places and ridges and lists later senses, but it does not establish the dates or semantic pathways among ‘high’, ‘excellent’, ‘esteemed’, ‘expensive’, ‘old’ and ‘loud’.
No component origin_relation classifications apply: the adopted analysis treats 高 as a whole pictographic graph, not a graph assembled from independently established semantic or phonetic components.

Xiaoxuetang's CC0 notice was verified, but a 高-specific query record and exact selected image URL were not available in rendered page results. Candidate links from Shuowen5 and ZDIC were inaccessible at image level, so no glyph asset with independently verified reuse terms is proposed. Local or page captions alone do not establish permission to mirror those images.

limitations.text: No image candidates were returned because actual image fetches failed and usable image-level provenance plus reuse terms were not established. The examined source descriptions identify oracle-bone and bronze candidates, but the image content and licensing could not be checked. This is not a claim that no historical glyph images exist.
